Both official pages explicitly support this trend; rate is distinct from population count.

assertions.assertion: Equity and inclusion progress is uneven
assertions.basis: Report documents differing country trajectories and gaps in location and wealth disparity reporting.
Live HTML digest differs; exact original snapshot and extraction method absent.

diagnosis: PASS on the substantive open-path proposition. Primary/lower-secondary/upper-secondary completion rose from 77/60/37 percent to 88/78/61 percent since 2000. UNESCO explicitly describes out-of-school rates as stagnant and discusses contextual equity measures and missing disparity reporting. The supplied overview snapshot digest does not match fetched HTML, with no historical snapshot bytes or extraction procedure available; the supplied sdg-4-scorecard URL returned 404. These provenance defects do not negate the proposition independently supported by the official 2026 report. No claim is made that anyone used this digest or benefited from it.
method: Independently fetched UNESCO https://www.unesco.org/gem-report/en and https://www.unesco.org/reports/gem-report/en/2026 on 2026-09-11. Read their education trends and equity discussion, rather than treating a matching digest as proof of the proposition. Verified claimant signature and claim_id using RFC 8785 and Ed25519, and reproduced the inline digest SHA-256. The report supports increasing completion, stagnant out-of-school rates, and uneven progress. This verifies the descriptive summary, not causal impact or independent accuracy of the underlying UNESCO estimates.
would_raise_confidence: A versioned report or archived snapshot dated on or before 2026-09-03, with a documented extraction procedure; direct disaggregated tables supporting the national-average interpretation. Evidence of readership would be needed for an impact claim.
